definition_en: the act of obeying a rule, law, or standard, or the state of meeting its requirements
core_image: 一把尺子贴着文件边缘，每一行都对齐刻度
scene: 审计员把一叠报关单铺在桌上，逐栏核对申报内容。The auditor checked every customs form to confirm full compliance with the new rules.
sceneCN: 这里 compliance 是「合规、符合规定」（第 2 个义项：达到规章要求的状态）；句意：审计员逐栏核对报关单，确认完全符合新规。

pos.zh: 名词：合规；遵从；服从；顺从

derivatives.zh: 由本词回溯动词形式，义为「遵守；服从；照做」
由 comply 加形容词后缀构成，义为「合规的；顺从的」
由否定前缀 non- 加本词构成，义为「不合规；未遵守」

senses.title: The act of obeying a rule
senses.definition: the act of following a law, order, rule, or request
senses.definitionCN: 遵守法律、命令、规则或要求的行为
senses.example: Compliance with the safety code is checked before every shipment.
senses.exampleCN: 每次发货前都会检查是否遵守安全规范。
senses.why: Compliance is built on Latin complere, to fill up: obeying a rule is filling its requirements to the brim.
senses.whyCN: compliance 来自拉丁语 complere「填满」：遵守规则就是把规则的要求填到满满当当。

senses.title: The state of meeting requirements
senses.definition: the condition of satisfying an official standard, regulation, or set of conditions
senses.definitionCN: 满足官方标准、法规或一组条件的状况
senses.example: The lab must prove compliance with the new hygiene standard.
senses.exampleCN: 实验室必须证明符合新的卫生标准。
senses.why: Once every condition is filled in, the object is in a state of compliance, like a form with no blank left.
senses.whyCN: 所有条件都填上之后，对象就处于合规状态，像一张没有空栏的表格。

senses.title: The business function of regulatory compliance
senses.definition: the work of making a company or institution follow laws and regulations, or the department that does this work
senses.definitionCN: 使公司或机构遵守法律法规的工作，或负责这项工作的部门
senses.example: She moved from the legal team to the compliance department last year.
senses.exampleCN: 她去年从法务团队调到了合规部门。
senses.why: Modern business turned the state of conformity into a permanent task: someone must keep filling the rules in.
senses.whyCN: 现代企业把「符合」这种状态变成长期任务：必须有人不断把规则填进去。

senses.title: Willingness to agree or cooperate
senses.definition: the tendency to agree to a request or to cooperate with another person
senses.definitionCN: 愿意答应请求或与他人合作的倾向
senses.example: The patient showed steady compliance with the treatment plan.
senses.exampleCN: 病人对治疗方案表现出稳定的配合。
senses.why: A request is also a container of expectations; compliance fills it by saying yes and then acting on it.
senses.whyCN: 请求也是一个装满期望的容器；compliance 用答应并照做把它填满。

senses.title: Excessive submissiveness
senses.definition: the tendency to obey others too readily, without question, often used with disapproval
senses.definitionCN: 过于轻易、不加质疑地服从他人，常带贬义
senses.example: Critics describe the board as a culture of quiet compliance.
senses.exampleCN: 批评者把董事会描述成一种沉默顺从的文化。
senses.why: The same filling can go too far: a person who fills every demand of others leaves no room for an own judgment.
senses.whyCN: 同样的「填满」也会过头：把别人的每个要求都填满，就没给自己的判断留下空间。

senses.title: The quality of yielding under pressure
senses.definition: the ability of a material or a body part to yield and expand under pressure, used in physics and medicine
senses.definitionCN: 材料或身体部位在压力下让位与扩张的能力，用于物理和医学
senses.example: Lung compliance falls when the tissue becomes stiff.
senses.exampleCN: 组织变硬时，肺的顺应性会下降。
senses.why: A compliant body yields to pressure instead of resisting it; technical use measures exactly how far it gives way.
senses.whyCN: compliant 的身体会顺从压力而不是抵抗；技术用法测的正是它让位了多少。

senses.title: In the phrase in compliance with
senses.definition: in the phrase in compliance with, in accordance with a rule, order, or standard
senses.definitionCN: 用于短语 in compliance with，表示按照规则、命令或标准
senses.example: All samples were stored in compliance with the safety rules.
senses.exampleCN: 所有样本都按安全规则存放。
senses.why: The phrase fixes compliance as the measure you follow: the rule is the line, and the action stays inside it.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语把合规固定成你遵循的尺度：规则是那条线，行为不能越出线外。

senses.title: Following medical advice
senses.definition: the degree to which a patient follows medical advice, takes medicine, or keeps a treatment schedule
senses.definitionCN: 病人遵循医嘱、按时服药或遵守治疗安排的程度
senses.example: Good compliance keeps the drug level steady in the blood.
senses.exampleCN: 良好的依从性让药物浓度在血液中保持稳定。
senses.why: Medicine took the general sense and narrowed it: the rule to obey is the prescription, and filling it means taking every dose.
senses.whyCN: 医学沿用一般含义并加以收窄：要遵守的规则是处方，填满它就是每一剂都按时服下。

intro.en: Compliance is the noun of comply, which came through Old French from the Latin verb complere, to fill up or fulfil.
intro.cn: compliance 是 comply 的名词形式；comply 经由古法语来自拉丁语动词 complere（填满、完成、履行）。

items.en: The verb plere means to fill, and it is the semantic seed of the whole family.
items.cn: 动词 plere 意为「填满」，是整个词族的意义起点。

items.en: Com- adds completeness to plere, giving complere, to fill up, complete, or fulfil a duty.
items.cn: com- 给 plere 加上「完全」，构成 complere，意为填满、完成或履行义务。

items.en: Old French complir means to fulfil or carry out, keeping the image of filling a duty to the end.
items.cn: 古法语 complir 意为履行、执行，保留了「把义务填到底」的意象。

items.en: The verb comply is recorded in English in the fourteenth century; the exact first date is uncertain.
items.cn: 动词 comply 于十四世纪见于英语；确切首见年代不确定。

items.en: The noun compliance is recorded later, naming the act or state of complying; the first date is uncertain.
items.cn: 名词 compliance 出现较晚，指遵从的行为或状态；首见年代不确定。

items.en: Regulation turned compliance into a named corporate function, with officers, audits, and formal programmes.
items.cn: 监管把 compliance 变成一项有名称的企业职能，配有合规官、审计与正式制度。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the Latin family of complere; the near-meaning group gathers words for obedience and conformity of different strength.
note.cn: 形近组收 complere 这一拉丁词族；近义组收表示服从与符合的词，强度各有不同。

entries.definition: To act in accordance with a rule, order, or request.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「遵守、服从、照做」，是本词的动词来源。

entries.definition: Obeying a rule or willing to agree; also used of a material that yields.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「合规的、顺从的」，也可指材料容易让位。

entries.definition: Eager to please others; it only looks similar and comes from Latin complacere, not from complere.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「殷勤的、讨人喜欢的」；只是拼写相近，词源不同，来自拉丁语 complacere。

entries.definition: The act of doing what a person in authority tells you to do.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「服从、听从」，强调对权威的听从。

entries.definition: Agreement with a standard, rule, or expected pattern of behaviour.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「符合、一致」，强调与标准或常规相合。

entries.definition: Faithful following of a rule, belief, or treatment plan.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「坚持、遵行」，强调持续不偏离地遵守。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Latin verb complere, the English word family, and the phrases the noun actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子使用真实的拉丁语动词 complere、英语词族，以及这个词实际出现的搭配。

normal.en: complere is to fill up, and compliance is the state of having filled every requirement of a rule.
normal.cn: complere 就是「填满」，compliance 是把规则要求逐条填满后的状态。

normal.en: Hold the family together: comply, compliant, compliance, and non-compliance.
normal.cn: 把词族串起来：comply、compliant、compliance、non-compliance。

normal.en: In compliance with the law means acting inside the line that the law draws.
normal.cn: in compliance with the law 意为在法律划出的线内行事。

normal.en: A compliance officer checks contracts and licences before a deal closes.
normal.cn: 合规官在交易完成前检查合同与执照。

normal.en: Non-compliance is the opposite label, and it is the one that brings fines.
normal.cn: non-compliance 是相反的标签，也正是招来罚款的那一个。

abstract.en: See a ruler laid along the edge of a page, with every line of text meeting the scale.
abstract.cn: 想象一把尺子贴着纸页边缘，每一行字都正好对齐刻度。

abstract.en: See a form with every box ticked and no blank left anywhere.
abstract.cn: 想象一张表格每个格子都已打勾，没有留下任何空栏。

abstract.en: See a clerk in a back office ticking a checklist of licences every month.
abstract.cn: 想象一名职员在后台办公室，每月逐项核对执照清单。

examples.en: The company hired a compliance officer after the inspection.
examples.cn: 检查之后，公司聘请了一位合规官。

examples.en: Non-compliance with the export rules can lead to heavy fines.
examples.cn: 不遵守出口规定可能招致高额罚款。

examples.en: The auditor asked for proof of compliance with the safety standard.
examples.cn: 审计员要求提供符合安全标准的证明。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「肯普莱恩斯」——把规章的每个格子都填满，就算合规；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 com-（一起、完全）+ plere（填满）→ complere（填满、完成、履行）→ 古法语 complir → 英语 comply（遵从、照做）；compliance 由 comply 加 -ance 构成，核心义「把要求填满做到」。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of compliance all come from one image, filling a container: a rule, a standard, a request, a prescription, or the pressure on a yielding body.
sensesIntro.cn: compliance 的八个义项都出自同一个意象——把容器填满：填的是规则、标准、请求、处方，或压在柔软身体上的压力。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a ruler is laid along the edge of a page, and every line of text meets the scale.
core.cn: 核心意象：一把尺子贴着纸页边缘，每一行字都对齐刻度。

branches.en: THE ACT: obeying a rule and granting a request are both ways of filling what another person asks.
branches.cn: 行为线：遵守规则与答应请求，都是把别人要求的东西填上。

branches.en: THE STATE: when no condition is left blank, the object is in compliance.
branches.cn: 状态线：当没有一个条件空着，对象就处于合规状态。

branches.en: THE INSTITUTION: a company keeps filling the rules as a permanent job with its own staff.
branches.cn: 机构线：企业把填规则变成一项有专人负责的长期工作。

branches.en: THE NARROW ENDS: filling every demand of others becomes submissiveness, while filling a prescription becomes medical adherence.
branches.cn: 收窄的两端：把别人的每个要求都填满会变成盲从，把处方填满则成为遵医嘱。

branches.en: THE TECHNICAL EDGES: a body yields under pressure, and the phrase in compliance with turns the noun into a measure of conduct.
branches.cn: 技术边缘：身体在压力下让位，而 in compliance with 这个短语把名词变成衡量行为的尺度。

intro.en: Compliance grows from the Latin verb complere, to fill up, and English builds the family with comply, compliant and the noun suffix -ance.
intro.cn: compliance 由拉丁语动词 complere（填满）发展而来，英语再用 comply、compliant 与名词后缀 -ance 扩展出这一词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin plere means to fill; com- adds completeness, so complere means to fill up, finish, and fulfil.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 plere 意为「填满」，com- 加上「完全」，于是 complere 表示填满、完成与履行。

items.example: The prefix adds the idea of fullness to the verb.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀给动词加上「满」的意思。

items.example: Plere supplies the filling image of the family.
items.exampleCN: plere 提供这一词族「填满」的意象。

items.example: Complere is the direct source of the English verb.
items.exampleCN: complere 是英语动词的直接来源。

items.example: Comply is the short English verb of the family.
items.exampleCN: comply 是这一词族中的英语短动词。

items.meaningCN: 状态或行为的名词后缀
items.example: The suffix -ance forms compliance from comply.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ance 把 comply 变成 compliance。

items.meaning: the act or state of obeying
items.example: Compliance keeps the noun sense of the Latin verb.
items.exampleCN: compliance 保留了拉丁语动词的名词含义。

items.example: Compliant describes a person or product that meets a rule.
items.exampleCN: compliant 描述符合规则的人或产品。

items.example: The suffix -ant forms compliant.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ant 构成 compliant。

items.example: The prefix non- forms non-compliance.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 non- 构成 non-compliance。

items.example: Complaisant looks like this family but comes from another Latin root.
items.exampleCN: complaisant 看似同族，其实来自另一个拉丁词根。

definition_en: money that a court orders a person or organization to pay to someone they have harmed or wronged
core_image: 法庭桌上的一叠钞票，被推给车被撞坏的一方
scene: 雨夜里两车相撞，修车行的报价单摊在桌上。The court ordered the driver to pay damages for the wrecked car.
sceneCN: 这里 damages 是「损害赔偿金」（第 1 个义项：法院判给受害方的金钱赔偿）；句意：法院判令那名司机为撞坏的汽车支付赔偿金。

pos.zh: 名词（法律复数）：损害赔偿金；损失赔偿

forms.label: 复数（本词为法律复数名词）

derivatives.zh: 由 damage 加 -ing 构成，义为「有害的；造成损害的」
由 damage 加 -ed 构成，义为「受损的；被损坏的」
由 damage 加 -able 构成，义为「易受损的；可被损坏的」

senses.title: Money awarded for a loss
senses.definition: money that a court orders a wrongdoer to pay to the person who suffered a loss
senses.definitionCN: 法院判令加害人向受损方支付的金钱
senses.example: The court awarded the workers damages for their unpaid wages.
senses.exampleCN: 法院判给工人被拖欠工资的损害赔偿金。
senses.why: Latin damnum is a loss; the plural damages names the money that stands in for the loss.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 damnum 是「损失」；复数 damages 指代替那笔损失的钱。

senses.title: Compensatory damages
senses.definition: damages intended to put the claimant back in the position held before the wrong, covering actual loss
senses.definitionCN: 旨在让索赔人回到不法行为发生前状态的赔偿金，填补实际损失
senses.example: Compensatory damages covered the cost of the ruined crop.
senses.exampleCN: 补偿性赔偿金填补了被毁作物的成本。
senses.why: If the loss can be measured, compensation is the sum that fills the hole it left.
senses.whyCN: 如果损失可以计量，补偿就是填平那个窟窿的金额。

senses.title: Punitive damages
senses.definition: damages awarded beyond the actual loss in order to punish the wrongdoer and discourage similar conduct
senses.definitionCN: 超出实际损失判给的赔偿金，用于惩罚加害人并遏制类似行为
senses.example: The jury added punitive damages because the fraud was deliberate.
senses.exampleCN: 由于欺诈是蓄意的，陪审团加判了惩罚性赔偿金。
senses.why: Damnum can also mean a penalty; when the loss alone is not enough to deter, the court adds a punishing sum.
senses.whyCN: damnum 也有「罚金」之义；当损失本身不足以威慑时，法院再加一笔惩罚性的钱。

senses.title: Nominal damages
senses.definition: a small symbolic sum awarded when a right was violated but no measurable loss was proved
senses.definitionCN: 权利确实被侵犯、但没有证明可计量损失时判给的象征性小额赔偿
senses.example: The court awarded nominal damages of one dollar for the trespass.
senses.exampleCN: 法院就非法侵入判给一美元名义赔偿金。
senses.why: A loss in law can be a lost right rather than lost money, so the court marks it with a token sum.
senses.whyCN: 法律上的损失也可以是失去权利而非失去金钱，因此法院用象征性金额把它记下。

senses.title: General damages
senses.definition: damages for loss that cannot be exactly counted, such as pain, suffering, or harm to reputation
senses.definitionCN: 对无法精确计算的损失判给的赔偿金，如疼痛、痛苦或名誉受损
senses.example: General damages were assessed for the injuries and the distress they caused.
senses.exampleCN: 法院就伤害及其造成的痛苦评定了一般损害赔偿金。
senses.why: Some losses have no receipt; the court estimates a sum that reflects the harm.
senses.whyCN: 有些损失没有发票；法院估算一笔反映该损害的金额。

senses.title: Special damages
senses.definition: damages for losses that can be calculated exactly, such as medical bills or lost earnings
senses.definitionCN: 对可以精确计算的损失判给的赔偿金，如医疗费或收入损失
senses.example: Special damages included the hospital bills and the lost salary.
senses.exampleCN: 特别损害赔偿金包括住院账单和损失的薪水。
senses.why: Where the loss leaves a paper trail, the claim must list each item and its amount.
senses.whyCN: 当损失留下纸面记录时，索赔必须逐项列出每一项及其金额。

senses.title: Liquidated damages
senses.definition: a sum agreed in advance in a contract as the compensation for a specified breach
senses.definitionCN: 合同中事先约定的、针对特定违约行为的赔偿金额
senses.example: Liquidated damages of ten thousand dollars were due for each late week.
senses.exampleCN: 每延迟一周就应支付一万美元的约定赔偿金。
senses.why: The parties count the loss before it happens and fix the sum, so no dispute over amount remains.
senses.whyCN: 当事人在损失发生前就估算好并固定金额，事后便不再为数额争执。

senses.title: Aggravated damages
senses.definition: extra damages awarded for the added distress caused by the way the wrong was committed
senses.definitionCN: 因不法行为的实施方式造成额外痛苦而加判的赔偿金
senses.example: Aggravated damages reflected the humiliating manner of the dismissal.
senses.exampleCN: 加重赔偿金反映了那次解雇带有侮辱性的方式。
senses.why: The manner of the wrong adds a second layer of loss, and the sum rises to answer it.
senses.whyCN: 不法行为的方式又添了一层损失，金额也随之提高来回应它。

intro.en: Damages is the legal plural of damage, which came through Old French from the Latin noun damnum, a loss or harm.
intro.cn: damages 是 damage 的法律复数形式；damage 经由古法语来自拉丁语名词 damnum（损失、损害）。

items.en: Damnum means loss, harm, or a fine, and it is the source of the whole word family.
items.cn: damnum 意为损失、损害，也指罚金，是整个词族的来源。

items.en: The adjective damnosus means causing loss or ruinous, already close to the modern adjective.
items.cn: 形容词 damnosus 意为造成损失的、破坏性的，已经接近现代形容词。

items.en: Old French damage carries the noun into French with the sense of loss and injury.
items.cn: 古法语 damage 把这一名词带入法语，含有损失与伤害之意。

items.en: The noun damage is recorded in English in the fourteenth century; the exact first date is uncertain.
items.cn: 名词 damage 于十四世纪见于英语；确切首见年代不确定。

items.en: Law makes the plural damages a name for the money awarded; the date of this specialization is uncertain.
items.cn: 法律把复数 damages 用作所判金钱的名称；这一专门化用法的年代不确定。

items.en: Modern courts sort damages into compensatory, nominal, punitive, general, special and other classes.
items.cn: 现代法院把损害赔偿金分为补偿性、名义、惩罚性、一般、特别等类别。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the ordinary damage family; the near-meaning group gathers other words for money paid because of a loss.
note.cn: 形近组收普通的 damage 词族；近义组收其他表示「因损失而付钱」的词。

entries.definition: Harm done to a thing or a person, or the noun for such harm.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「损害、损坏」，指对物或人造成的伤害，是本词的单数来源。

entries.definition: Causing harm or a bad effect.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「有害的、造成损害的」，由 damage 加 -ing 构成。

entries.definition: Harmed or broken, used of things and sometimes of people.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「受损的、被损坏的」，由 damage 加 -ed 构成。

entries.definition: Money paid to make up for a loss, an injury, or work done.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「补偿、赔偿金」，范围比 damages 宽，不限于法院判决。

entries.definition: Money or other action taken to repair a wrong, often between states.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「赔偿、修复」，语气正式，常用于国家之间。

entries.definition: The act of giving back what was taken or restoring a previous position.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「返还、恢复原状」，指把取走之物归还或恢复原状。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Latin noun damnum, the legal phrases, and the ordinary damage family.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子使用真实的拉丁语名词 damnum、法律搭配，以及普通的 damage 词族。

normal.en: damnum is a loss, and damages are the money that replaces the loss.
normal.cn: damnum 是「损失」，damages 就是替代这笔损失的钱。

normal.en: The singular damage names the harm; the legal plural damages names the money.
normal.cn: 单数 damage 指损害本身，法律复数 damages 指那笔钱。

normal.en: A court awards damages, a claimant claims them, and a wrongdoer pays them.
normal.cn: 法院判给损害赔偿金，索赔人索取它，加害人支付它。

normal.en: Compensatory damages try to make the claimant whole again.
normal.cn: 补偿性赔偿金努力让索赔人恢复到完整状态。

normal.en: Punitive damages are added to punish, not to replace a loss.
normal.cn: 惩罚性赔偿金是为惩罚而加判的，不是用来填补损失。

abstract.en: See a judge sliding a stack of notes across the bench toward the person who lost a car.
abstract.cn: 想象法官把一叠钞票从审判席推向那位失去汽车的人。

abstract.en: See a cracked cup being filled and mended until it holds water again.
abstract.cn: 想象一只裂开的杯子被填补、粘好，直到又能盛水。

abstract.en: See a hand adding an extra coin to a bill, not to pay for the goods but to punish the careless shop.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手在账单上多放一枚硬币，不是为了付货款，而是为了惩罚马虎的店家。

examples.en: The jury awarded the family one million dollars in damages.
examples.cn: 陪审团判给这个家庭一百万美元损害赔偿金。

examples.en: The seller must pay damages for the faulty goods.
examples.cn: 卖方必须就缺陷商品支付损害赔偿金。

examples.en: Liquidated damages were fixed at ten thousand dollars for each late week.
examples.cn: 每延迟一周的约定赔偿金被定为一万美元。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「丹米吉兹」——损失账单上的数字，最后变成法庭判给的钱；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 damnum（损失、损害，也指罚金）→ 古法语 damage（损失）→ 英语 damage；法律把它的复数 damages 专门用作「以金钱填补损失的赔偿金」。同族还有 damnare（判罚、使人受损）与 damnificus（造成损失的），核心义「使人遭受损失」。

sensesIntro.en: The eight senses divide the legal money award by purpose: to replace a loss, to mark a right, to punish, to fix a sum in advance, or to answer an added injury.
sensesIntro.cn: 这八个义项按目的划分这笔法律款项：填补损失、标记权利、实施惩罚、事先固定金额，或回应额外伤害。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a stack of notes on the court bench is pushed toward the person whose car was wrecked.
core.cn: 核心意象：审判席上的一叠钞票被推向那位汽车被撞坏的人。

branches.en: THE WHOLE: the plural names the money that takes the place of a loss.
branches.cn: 总称线：复数形式指替代损失的那笔钱。

branches.en: THE MEASURE: compensation splits loss into what can be counted and what must be estimated.
branches.cn: 计量线：补偿把损失分成可精确计算与必须估算的两类。

branches.en: THE PENALTY: punitive damages add punishment to the payment.
branches.cn: 惩罚线：惩罚性赔偿金在付款之外加上惩罚。

branches.en: THE MARKS: nominal and aggravated damages mark a right or an added injury rather than a price.
branches.cn: 标记线：名义赔偿与加重赔偿标记的是权利或额外伤害，而不是价格。

branches.en: THE CONTRACT: liquidated damages fix the sum before the breach happens.
branches.cn: 合同线：约定赔偿金在违约发生之前就把金额固定下来。

intro.en: Damages sits at the centre of a Latin family built on damnum, loss: damage, damaging, damaged, damageable and the legal plural damages.
intro.cn: damages 位于以 damnum（损失）为核心的拉丁词族中央：damage、damaging、damaged、damageable 与法律复数 damages 都由此展开。

latinIntro.en: Latin damnum means loss, harm, or a fine; damnare means to condemn or inflict loss, and damnificus means causing loss.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 damnum 意为损失、损害或罚金；damnare 意为判罚、使受损，damnificus 意为造成损失的。

items.example: Damnum is the root noun of the whole family.
items.exampleCN: damnum 是整个词族的根名词。

items.example: Damnare is formed on the same loss root.
items.exampleCN: damnare 由同一个「损失」词根构成。

items.example: Damnosus describes something that brings loss.
items.exampleCN: damnosus 描述带来损失的事物。

items.example: Damnificus joins the loss root with a making suffix.
items.exampleCN: damnificus 把「损失」词根与「致使」后缀结合在一起。

items.example: Damage is the everyday English noun.
items.exampleCN: damage 是日常英语名词。

items.example: Damages is the legal plural of damage.
items.exampleCN: damages 是 damage 的法律复数。

items.example: Damaging is formed with the suffix -ing.
items.exampleCN: damaging 由后缀 -ing 构成。

items.example: Damaged is formed with the suffix -ed.
items.exampleCN: damaged 由后缀 -ed 构成。

items.example: Damageable adds the suffix -able to damage.
items.exampleCN: damageable 在 damage 后加后缀 -able。

items.example: The suffix -age helped shape damage in Old French.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -age 在古法语中参与构成 damage。

definition_zh: 补偿；赔偿；赔偿保证；免责保障
definition_en: a promise to compensate someone for a loss or to protect them from liability, or the money paid under such a promise
core_image: 一个人把对方手里的账单接过来，替他把钱付清
scene: 仓库失火后，保险勘察员站在焦黑的货架间核对清单。The policy gave the owner an indemnity for the burned stock.
sceneCN: 这里 indemnity 是「保险赔偿」（第 3 个义项：保险人就承保损失作出的补偿）；句意：保单为被烧毁的存货给业主提供了一笔赔偿。

pos.zh: 名词：补偿；赔偿；赔偿保证；免责保障

derivatives.zh: 由本词加动词后缀构成，义为「赔偿；使免受损失或责任」
由 indemnify 加名词后缀构成，义为「赔偿；免责保障」
由 indemnify 加过去分词后缀构成，义为「已获赔偿的；受保障的」

senses.title: The promise to cover a loss
senses.definition: a promise by one party to compensate another for a specified loss or damage
senses.definitionCN: 一方承诺就特定损失或损害向另一方作出补偿
senses.example: The parent company gave an indemnity to cover the debts of the subsidiary.
senses.exampleCN: 母公司提供了赔偿保证，以承担子公司的债务。
senses.why: Latin in- means not and damnum means loss, so indemnity begins as the state of being without loss.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 in- 表示「不」，damnum 表示「损失」，所以 indemnity 起初指「不受损失」的状态。

senses.title: The money paid under a promise
senses.definition: the sum paid to make good a loss under such a promise
senses.definitionCN: 依据这类承诺为填补损失而支付的款项
senses.example: The builder received an indemnity for the delay in delivery.
senses.exampleCN: 建筑商就交货延迟获得了一笔补偿金。
senses.why: The promise becomes concrete as money: what was lost is weighed and paid back in cash.
senses.whyCN: 承诺落实为金钱：损失被折算成数额，再用现金补回去。

senses.title: Insurance compensation
senses.definition: payment by an insurer to restore the insured to the financial position held before the loss
senses.definitionCN: 保险人支付的款项，使被保险人回到损失发生前的经济状况
senses.example: The insurer settled the claim with an indemnity equal to the market value.
senses.exampleCN: 保险人以相当于市场价值的赔偿结清了索赔。
senses.why: Insurance is the purest form of the idea: a pool of money keeps the insured person free from the loss.
senses.whyCN: 保险是这一观念最纯粹的形式：一笔共同资金让被保险人免受损失。

senses.title: Protection against liability
senses.definition: a contractual promise to protect another party from legal liability or the cost of claims
senses.definitionCN: 合同中的承诺，保护另一方免受法律责任或索赔成本
senses.example: The contractor accepted a broad indemnity in favour of the client.
senses.exampleCN: 承包商接受了有利于客户的一项宽泛免责保障。
senses.why: Loss can also be a legal burden; keeping a party free from loss means keeping the claim off that party.
senses.whyCN: 损失也可以是法律负担；让一方不受损失，就是把索赔挡在它之外。

senses.title: An indemnity clause
senses.definition: a term in a contract that sets out who must cover losses and claims arising from the deal
senses.definitionCN: 合同中的条款，规定由谁承担交易引起的损失与索赔
senses.example: The indemnity in clause eight survives the end of the agreement.
senses.exampleCN: 第八条中的赔偿条款在协议结束后仍然有效。
senses.why: A promise needs a place in the text, so the clause is the promise written down and given a boundary.
senses.whyCN: 承诺需要在文本中有个位置，条款就是写下来并被划定了边界的承诺。

senses.title: A letter or deed of indemnity
senses.definition: a document in which a person or bank promises to cover a loss, often used to release goods without the usual papers
senses.definitionCN: 个人或银行承诺承担损失的书面文件，常用于在缺少常规单据时放行货物
senses.example: The bank issued a letter of indemnity so the cargo could be released.
senses.exampleCN: 银行出具了赔偿保证书，使货物得以放行。
senses.why: When the usual papers are missing, the document itself carries the promise and lets the goods move.
senses.whyCN: 常规单据缺失时，这份文件本身承载承诺，让货物得以流转。

senses.title: Exemption from penalty
senses.definition: a grant of freedom from a penalty or from prosecution, especially by law
senses.definitionCN: 免于处罚或免于起诉的授予，尤指由法律规定
senses.example: An act of indemnity protected the officials from prosecution.
senses.exampleCN: 一项赦免法使那些官员免于起诉。
senses.why: The old legal sense extends the image from loss of money to loss of freedom: indemnity removes the threatened penalty.
senses.whyCN: 古老的法律义把意象从金钱损失扩展到自由损失：indemnity 撤除了悬在头上的处罚。

senses.title: A war indemnity
senses.definition: money that a defeated state is required to pay to the victor to cover the costs and losses of war
senses.definitionCN: 战败国被要求向战胜国支付的、用于弥补战争成本与损失的款项
senses.example: The treaty fixed the war indemnity at three billion francs.
senses.exampleCN: 条约把战争赔款定为三十亿法郎。
senses.why: Between states the loss is measured in whole economies, and the payment that covers it is still called an indemnity.
senses.whyCN: 国家之间的损失以整个经济来计量，而弥补这笔损失的付款仍然叫 indemnity。

intro.en: Indemnity is Latin in- plus damnum, loss: the word starts as freedom from loss and grows into the promise that keeps someone free from it.
intro.cn: indemnity 是拉丁语 in- 加 damnum（损失）：这个词从「不受损失」起步，发展为让人免受损失的那项承诺。

items.en: Damnum means loss or harm, and it is the base of the whole family.
items.cn: damnum 意为损失或损害，是整个词族的基础。

items.en: In- negates damnum: indemnis means unharmed, free from loss.
items.cn: in- 否定 damnum：indemnis 意为未受损害的、不受损失的。

items.en: Indemnitas names security against loss and, in law, exemption from penalty.
items.cn: indemnitas 指免受损失的保障，在法律中也指免于处罚。

items.en: The noun passes into French as indemnite, keeping both the security and the exemption senses.
items.cn: 这个名词以 indemnite 的形式进入法语，同时保留保障与免罚两种含义。

items.en: Indemnity is recorded in English in the fifteenth century; the exact first date is uncertain.
items.cn: indemnity 于十五世纪见于英语；确切首见年代不确定。

items.en: Insurance and commercial contracts turn indemnity into a standard promise to cover another party.
items.cn: 保险与商业合同把 indemnity 变成替另一方承担损失的标准承诺。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the English family built on indemnify; the near-meaning group gathers other ways of covering a loss.
note.cn: 形近组收围绕 indemnify 构成的英语词族；近义组收其他弥补损失的方式。

entries.definition: To compensate someone for a loss or to protect them from liability.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「赔偿、使免受损失或责任」，是本词的动词形式。

entries.definition: The act of compensating a loss or protecting a party from claims.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「赔偿行为、免责保障」，由 indemnify 加名词后缀构成。

entries.definition: Compensated for a loss, or protected against a claim.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「已获赔偿的、受保障的」，是 indemnify 的过去分词形式。

entries.definition: Money paid to make up for a loss, an injury, or work done.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「补偿、赔偿金」，是一般用语，不必然含合同承诺。

entries.definition: A contract in which a company covers a specified loss in return for regular payments.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「保险」，指以定期付费换取承保损失的合同。

entries.definition: A promise that something will be done or that a product will work, often backed by a repair or refund.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「保证、担保」，承诺某事一定做到或商品一定可用，常以维修或退款作后盾。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Latin parts in- and damnum, the English family, and the legal phrases the noun appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子使用真实的拉丁语成分 in- 与 damnum、英语词族，以及这个词实际出现的法律搭配。

normal.en: in- means not and damnum means loss, so indemnity is the promise that keeps a loss away.
normal.cn: in- 是「不」，damnum 是「损失」，所以 indemnity 是让损失不落到你身上的承诺。

normal.en: The verb is indemnify, the act is indemnification, and the protected party is indemnified.
normal.cn: 动词是 indemnify，行为是 indemnification，受保障的一方是 indemnified。

normal.en: An indemnity clause decides who pays when a third party brings a claim.
normal.cn: indemnity clause 决定第三方提出索赔时由谁付钱。

normal.en: A letter of indemnity lets goods move when the usual papers are missing.
normal.cn: letter of indemnity 让货物在缺少常规单据时仍可放行。

normal.en: In history, an act of indemnity wipes out a threatened penalty rather than a bill.
normal.cn: 在历史上，act of indemnity 抹掉的是悬着的处罚，而不是一张账单。

abstract.en: See a hand taking a bill out of another hand and paying it at the counter.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手从另一只手里接过账单，替他在柜台付清。

abstract.en: See a cheque covering the exact cost of a burned shelf.
abstract.cn: 想象一张支票正好覆盖被烧毁货架的成本。

abstract.en: See a wide umbrella held over a warehouse while the rain pours down.
abstract.cn: 想象大雨倾盆时，一把大伞撑在仓库上方。

examples.en: The contract contains an indemnity clause covering third-party claims.
examples.cn: 合同中有一条涵盖第三方索赔的赔偿条款。

examples.en: The insurer paid an indemnity for the flooded warehouse.
examples.cn: 保险人为被淹的仓库支付了一笔赔偿。

examples.en: The defeated country was forced to pay a heavy war indemnity.
examples.cn: 战败国被迫支付巨额战争赔款。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「因登米提」——把损失挡在门外，账单由别人接过去付清；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 in-（不、无）+ damnum（损失）→ indemnis（未受损失的）→ indemnitas（免受损失、免罚）→ 古法语 indemnité → 英语 indemnity；核心义「使人不受损失」。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of indemnity apply one promise, to keep a person free from loss: a contract promise, a payment, insurance, protection from liability, a clause, a document, exemption from penalty, and a war payment.
sensesIntro.cn: indemnity 的八个义项都围绕同一项承诺——让人免受损失：合同承诺、实际付款、保险、责任保障、条款、文书、免罚与战争赔款。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one person takes the bill from another hand and pays it at the counter.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个人从对方手里接过账单，替他在柜台付清。

branches.en: THE PROMISE: a spoken promise and a written letter both carry the same undertaking.
branches.cn: 承诺线：口头承诺与书面保证书承载的是同一项承担。

branches.en: THE MONEY: the promise is cashed as a payment, and insurance is its most organised form.
branches.cn: 金钱线：承诺兑现为付款，保险则是它最有组织的形式。

branches.en: THE LIABILITY LINE: contract terms shift claims away from the protected party.
branches.cn: 责任线：合同条款把索赔从受保障一方身上移开。

branches.en: THE PENALTY: the old legal sense removes punishment rather than paying a bill.
branches.cn: 处罚线：古老的法律义撤除的是处罚，而不是支付账单。

branches.en: THE STATE: a defeated country pays for war losses on the same pattern.
branches.cn: 国家线：战败国按同样的模式为战争损失付钱。

intro.en: Indemnity is Latin in- plus damnum, and English adds indemnify, indemnification and the adjective indemnified around it.
intro.cn: indemnity 是拉丁语 in- 加 damnum，英语围绕它扩展出 indemnify、indemnification 与形容词 indemnified。

latinIntro.en: Latin in- means not, and damnum means loss; indemnis is unharmed, and indemnitas is security against loss.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 in- 意为「不」，damnum 意为「损失」；indemnis 是未受损害的，indemnitas 是免受损失的保障。

items.example: The prefix turns loss into freedom from loss.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把「损失」变成「不受损失」。

items.example: Damnum supplies the loss at the centre of the word.
items.exampleCN: damnum 提供这个词中央的「损失」。

items.meaningCN: 未受损害的；不受损失的
items.example: Indemnis is the adjective made of the prefix and the noun.
items.exampleCN: indemnis 是由前缀与名词构成的形容词。

items.example: Indemnitas is the direct Latin source of indemnity.
items.exampleCN: indemnitas 是 indemnity 的直接拉丁语来源。

items.example: The suffix -itas forms abstract nouns.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -itas 构成抽象名词。

items.meaning: a promise to cover a loss
items.example: Indemnity keeps the Latin noun sense.
items.exampleCN: indemnity 保留拉丁语名词的含义。

items.meaning: to compensate for loss, protect from liability
items.example: Indemnify is the verb of the family.
items.exampleCN: indemnify 是这一词族的动词。

items.example: The suffix -ify forms indemnify.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ify 构成 indemnify。

items.example: Indemnification names the act rather than the promise.
items.exampleCN: indemnification 指的是行为，而不是承诺本身。

latinEntries.meaningCN: 未受损害的；不受损失的

definition_zh: 保证；担保；保修；保证条款
definition_en: a promise, especially in a sale or contract, that a product or condition is as stated and will be repaired or replaced if it fails
core_image: 商品包装里夹着一张卡片，上面写着「坏了就换」
scene: 新买的咖啡机第二周就漏水，说明书最后一页夹着一张卡片。The warranty covers free repairs for two years.
sceneCN: 这里 warranty 是「保修承诺」（第 1 个义项：卖方对商品质量的书面保证）；句意：这张保修承诺涵盖两年的免费维修。

pos.zh: 名词：保证；担保；保修；保证条款

derivatives.zh: 同源基础词，义为「授权令；令状」或「保证；使有正当理由」
由本词加表示「人」的后缀构成，义为「保证人；担保人」
由 warrant 加过去分词后缀构成，义为「有正当理由的；有保证的」

senses.title: The promise to repair or replace a product
senses.definition: a promise by a seller or maker to repair or replace a product that fails within a stated period
senses.definitionCN: 卖方或制造者承诺在约定期间内修理或更换出故障的产品
senses.example: The warranty covers parts but not the labour charge.
senses.exampleCN: 保修涵盖零件，但不含人工费。
senses.why: Warant is an Old French pledge; a warranty is that pledge attached to a thing, so the thing can be brought back if it breaks.
senses.whyCN: warant 是古法语中的「担保」；warranty 就是附着在物品上的那项担保，物品坏了可以拿回来。

senses.title: A promise about quality
senses.definition: a contractual promise that goods or work meet a stated standard of quality
senses.definitionCN: 合同中的承诺，保证货物或工程达到约定的质量标准
senses.example: The warranty required the steel to resist salt water.
senses.exampleCN: 质量保证条款要求这种钢材能抗海水腐蚀。
senses.why: The pledge can be made about a standard rather than a repair: the seller answers for the quality of what is handed over.
senses.whyCN: 担保可以针对标准而不是维修：卖方要为交出去的东西的质量负责。

senses.title: An express warranty
senses.definition: a warranty stated in words, whether in the contract, the advertising, or on a label
senses.definitionCN: 以文字明确表达的保证，可写在合同中，也可出现在广告或标签上
senses.example: The brochure created an express warranty about the battery life.
senses.exampleCN: 产品手册就电池续航作出了一项明示保证。
senses.why: The pledge becomes express when it is put into words that a buyer can point to later.
senses.whyCN: 当担保被写成买方日后可以指认的文字时，它就成了明示保证。

senses.title: An implied warranty
senses.definition: a warranty read into a sale by law even though no one stated it, such as that goods are fit for their ordinary use
senses.definitionCN: 法律虽未言明却读入买卖中的保证，例如货物适合其通常用途
senses.example: An implied warranty protects buyers when a kettle cannot boil water safely.
senses.exampleCN: 当水壶无法安全烧水时，默示保证会保护买家。
senses.why: Law supplies the pledge that the parties forget to speak: a sale carries certain promises whether or not they are written.
senses.whyCN: 法律补上当事人忘了说出口的担保：一次买卖自带某些承诺，无论是否写下来。

senses.title: A warranty of title
senses.definition: a promise that the seller owns the goods and has the right to sell them free of claims by others
senses.definitionCN: 卖方承诺其拥有货物，并有权在不受他人主张限制的情况下出售
senses.example: The warranty of title failed because a bank held a claim on the machine.
senses.exampleCN: 由于银行对该机器享有主张，这项权利担保没有成立。
senses.why: The pledge can cover ownership itself: the seller guarantees that the thing is his to give.
senses.whyCN: 担保可以覆盖所有权本身：卖方保证这件东西确实归他处分。

senses.title: A warranty deed
senses.definition: a deed by which the seller of land guarantees the title and promises to defend it against claims
senses.definitionCN: 土地出卖人据此担保所有权并承诺抵御他人主张的契据
senses.example: The land was transferred by a warranty deed.
senses.exampleCN: 这块土地通过保证契据转让。
senses.why: Land needs a stronger pledge than goods, so the promise is sealed in a deed that can be enforced for years.
senses.whyCN: 土地需要比商品更强的担保，于是这项承诺被封进一份多年可执行的契据。

senses.title: The warranty period or service
senses.definition: the period during which a warranty applies, or the repair service given under it
senses.definitionCN: 保证适用的期间，或据此提供的维修服务
senses.example: The laptop is still within its warranty, so the screen will be replaced.
senses.exampleCN: 这台笔记本仍在保修期内，所以屏幕会被更换。
senses.why: The pledge has a clock attached: the promise lasts for a set time, and people name that time by the promise itself.
senses.whyCN: 这项担保挂着一只时钟：承诺只持续一段固定时间，人们便用承诺本身来称呼那段时间。

senses.title: A warranty in insurance
senses.definition: a promise by an insured person about a fact or condition that must remain true for the insurance to stay valid
senses.definitionCN: 被保险人就某项事实或状况作出的承诺，该事实须持续真实，保险才继续有效
senses.example: A breach of the warranty about the alarm system let the insurer refuse the claim.
senses.exampleCN: 违反关于警报系统的保证，使保险人得以拒绝赔付。
senses.why: Insurance uses the same pledge as a condition: the insured promises that a fact is true, and the cover depends on it.
senses.whyCN: 保险把同样的担保当作条件：被保险人承诺某项事实为真，保障能否成立取决于它。

intro.en: Warranty came into English through Anglo-Norman French from Old French warant, a pledge or guarantor, and it is Germanic in origin rather than Latin.
intro.cn: warranty 经由盎格鲁-诺曼法语进入英语，来自古法语 warant（担保、保证人），其源头属日耳曼语而非拉丁语。

items.en: The reconstructed verb warjan means to guard or defend; the reconstruction is standard, though the exact form is not attested.
items.cn: 一般认为原始日耳曼语动词 warjan 意为守卫、保护；这一重构形式是通行的，但确切词形并无文献记录。

items.en: Frankish warjan, a Germanic dialect form, is generally thought to have passed into Old French. Details of the transfer remain uncertain.
items.cn: 一般认为法兰克语 warjan 这一日耳曼方言形式传入了古法语；具体传播细节仍不确定。

items.en: Warantir means to guarantee or protect, and its participle warant names a guarantor or a pledge.
items.cn: warantir 意为担保、保护，其分词 warant 指保证人或担保物。

items.en: Legal French warantie names a promise that a thing is as stated, and it enters English law through Anglo-Norman.
items.cn: 法律法语 warantie 指「保证某物如所述」的承诺，经由盎格鲁-诺曼语进入英国法。

items.en: Warranty is recorded in English from the fourteenth century in the legal sense; the exact first date is uncertain.
items.cn: warranty 于十四世纪以法律义见于英语；确切首见年代不确定。

items.en: The consumer sense grows in the twentieth century, alongside warranties in insurance and land law.
items.cn: 消费者意义上的保修在二十世纪发展起来，与保险法和土地法中的保证并行。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the English family of warrant; the near-meaning group gathers other promises that back a product or a deal.
note.cn: 形近组收 warrant 这一英语词族；近义组收其他为商品或交易作后盾的承诺。

entries.definition: A document that gives official permission for an action, or a verb meaning to justify.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「授权令、令状」，作动词时义为「使有正当理由」，是本词的直接来源。

entries.definition: A person or company that gives a warranty.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「保证人、担保人」，由 warrant 加表示人的后缀构成。

entries.definition: Justified by facts, or covered by a warranty.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「有正当理由的、有保证的」，是 warrant 的过去分词形式。

entries.definition: A promise that something will be done or that a product will work, often backed by repair or refund.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「保证、担保」，承诺某事一定做到或商品一定可用，常以维修或退款作后盾。

entries.definition: A formal binding promise, especially one written into a deed or a contract.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「契约、约款」，指正式且有约束力的承诺，常写入契据或合同。

entries.definition: A statement made to give someone confidence that something is true or will happen.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「保证、确信」，指为让对方放心而作出的陈述，语气正式。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Old French pledge warant, the English family, and the phrases the noun appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子使用真实的古法语担保词 warant、英语词族，以及这个词实际出现的搭配。

normal.en: Warant is the Old French pledge, and a warranty is that pledge written into a sale.
normal.cn: warant 是古法语中的担保，warranty 就是把这项担保写进一次买卖。

normal.en: The family runs warrant, warranty, warrantor, and the adjective warranted.
normal.cn: 这一词族包括 warrant、warranty、warrantor 与形容词 warranted。

normal.en: Under warranty means the seller must still fix the product.
normal.cn: under warranty 意为卖方仍须负责修理这件产品。

normal.en: An express warranty is spoken or printed; an implied warranty is supplied by law.
normal.cn: 明示保证是说出口或印出来的，默示保证则由法律补上。

normal.en: A breach of warranty can end in damages rather than a repair.
normal.cn: 违反保证条款的结果可能是赔偿金，而不是一次维修。

abstract.en: See a card tucked into a box, stamped with a short promise to replace the goods if they break.
abstract.cn: 想象一张卡片塞进包装盒，上面印着一句「坏了就换」的短承诺。

abstract.en: See a seal pressed onto a contract, promising that the steel will not rust.
abstract.cn: 想象一枚印章压在合同上，保证这种钢材不会生锈。

abstract.en: See the same promise printed in large letters on a brochure at the counter.
abstract.cn: 想象同一句承诺用大字印在柜台旁的产品手册上。

examples.en: The laptop is still under warranty, so the repair is free.
examples.cn: 这台笔记本仍在保修期内，所以维修免费。

examples.en: The seller gave a warranty that the machine had no hidden defects.
examples.cn: 卖方作出保证，称这台机器没有隐藏缺陷。

examples.en: A breach of warranty may entitle the buyer to damages.
examples.cn: 违反保证条款可能使买方有权获得损害赔偿金。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「沃伦提」——像把一句「坏了就换」的承诺塞进包装盒；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 古法语 warant（保证人、担保）与 warantir（担保、保护）→ 盎格鲁-诺曼法语 warantie → 英语 warranty；一般认为更早的来源是法兰克语 warjan（保护、守卫），属日耳曼语源，并非拉丁词根，核心义「为某物作担保、把它护住」。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of warranty all attach a pledge to something: a product, a standard, spoken words, a legal implication, a title, a deed, a period of cover, or an insured fact.
sensesIntro.cn: warranty 的八个义项都把一项担保附着在某物上：商品、质量标准、明示文字、法律默示、所有权、契据、保修期间，或被保险的事实。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a card tucked into a product box carries one promise: if it breaks, it is replaced.
core.cn: 核心意象：塞进商品包装盒的一张卡片写着同一句承诺——坏了就换。

branches.en: THE PRODUCT: the pledge is attached to a thing that can be repaired or replaced.
branches.cn: 商品线：担保附着在一件可以修理或更换的物品上。

branches.en: THE QUALITY: the pledge can answer for a standard, and it may be express or implied.
branches.cn: 质量线：担保可以为某项标准负责，且可以是明示或默示的。

branches.en: THE TITLE: ownership and land need a pledge that is sealed and enforceable.
branches.cn: 权利线：所有权与土地需要一项被封印、可执行的担保。

branches.en: THE CLOCK: the promise lasts for a set period, and the period takes the name of the promise.
branches.cn: 时间线：承诺持续一段固定期间，而这段时间反过来用了承诺的名字。

branches.en: THE INSURED FACT: insurance turns the pledge into a condition of cover.
branches.cn: 保险线：保险把这项担保变成保障成立的条件。

intro.en: Warranty grows from the Old French pledge warant, and English builds warrant, warrantor and warranted around it with ordinary suffixes.
intro.cn: warranty 由古法语担保词 warant 发展而来，英语再用普通后缀扩展出 warrant、warrantor 与 warranted。

latinIntro.en: Warranty has no Latin root: it comes from Old French warant and Anglo-Norman warantie, generally traced to Frankish warjan, to protect. Medieval Latin borrowed the word instead of giving it.
latinIntro.cn: warranty 没有拉丁词根：它来自古法语 warant 与盎格鲁-诺曼法语 warantie，一般认为可上溯到法兰克语 warjan（保护）。中世纪拉丁语是借用这个词，而不是它的来源。

items.example: Warant is the pledge at the centre of the word.
items.exampleCN: warant 是这个词中央的「担保」。

items.example: Warantir is the verb that stands behind the noun.
items.exampleCN: warantir 是支撑这个名词的动词。

items.example: Warantie carries the word into English law.
items.exampleCN: warantie 把这个词带入英国法。

items.meaning: a document that authorizes an action
items.example: Warrant keeps the official meaning of the family.
items.exampleCN: warrant 保留这一词族的官方文书含义。

items.meaning: a promise about goods or title
items.example: Warranty is the noun used in sales and land law.
items.exampleCN: warranty 是买卖法与土地法中使用的名词。

items.meaning: a person who gives a warranty
items.example: Warrantor is formed with the suffix -or.
items.exampleCN: warrantor 由后缀 -or 构成。

items.meaningCN: 表示做某事的人的名词后缀
items.example: The suffix -or forms warrantor.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -or 构成 warrantor。

items.example: The suffix -y helps form warranty from warrant.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -y 帮助从 warrant 构成 warranty。

items.meaningCN: 有正当理由的；有保证的
items.example: Warranted is the past participle used as an adjective.
items.exampleCN: warranted 是过去分词用作形容词。
